note: All cases target the disposable PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev, id 70844de4-391c-4002-ac3c-6f1e21e4ecd3) so runs never touch the real backlog. Fixtures: NEX-129 daemon loop (unready, mid-ICE, ENABLER), NEX-130 assembly (ready), NEX-131 CI PATH fix (ready, small, time-sensitive), NEX-132 dep-ordering (unready), NEX-133 rename cutover (partial; quiet-window CHORE), NEX-134 gh-304 (ready; dedup target), NEX-135 board-intake (ready; blockedBy NEX-129 — the dependency fixture for case 6). Workflow states for the lane cases (6-7): NEX-135 is mis-filed in Todo despite being blockedBy NEX-129 (demote target); NEX-131 is ready + unblocked but sitting in Backlog (promote target); NEX-130 is correctly in Todo; all others in Backlog.

evals.prompt: Prioritize the backlog in the PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev team) in Linear and set the issue priorities.
evals.expected_output: A stack rank with a visible ICE score (Impact, Confidence, Ease and the product) per issue, each mapped to a Linear priority bucket, followed by proposed priority writes that wait for confirmation before touching Linear.
expectations: Shows a per-issue ICE breakdown with Impact, Confidence, and Ease values AND the multiplied score, not just a bare ordering
Maps each issue to a Linear priority level (Urgent/High/Medium/Low or 1-4)
Proposes the priority writes and explicitly waits for user confirmation instead of calling save_issue immediately
Reads the live PM-Sandbox issues before proposing, rather than assuming
Does NOT compute RICE or WSJF for these individual issues (uses ICE as the default single-scorer framework)

evals.prompt: A new bug is proposed for the PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev): 'github client throws on a 304 from gh api instead of treating it as unchanged'. Triage it.
evals.expected_output: A triage decision that separates severity from priority, searches existing PM-Sandbox issues for a duplicate (finds NEX-134) before creating anything, and gives an accept/defer/delete call with a reason — all proposed before any Linear write.
expectations: Distinguishes severity from priority explicitly rather than conflating them into one number
Searches existing issues for a possible duplicate before proposing to create anything, and surfaces the near-duplicate (NEX-134)
Gives an explicit accept / defer / delete decision with a stated reason
Proposes any label/priority/relation writes and waits for confirmation before executing

evals.prompt: Write a Linear story in the PM-Sandbox project for adding automatic retry-with-backoff to the github read client.
evals.expected_output: A story that is a vertical slice with a user/operator-facing outcome, has 3+ testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, is scoped to a single AI build session, and is proposed as a Linear issue before being created.
expectations: Frames the story as a vertical slice with a user- or operator-facing outcome, not a component/task like 'add a retry function'
Includes at least 3 testable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form
Explicitly checks or states that the story is sized to complete in one AI build session (splits or flags it if not)
Proposes the issue for confirmation before calling save_issue

evals.prompt: The PM-Sandbox project has a pile of backlog issues but no roadmap. Plan one in Linear.
evals.expected_output: A Now/Next/Later roadmap organized by decreasing certainty, mapped onto Linear initiatives/projects, that flags the PM-Sandbox project is not linked to an initiative, and proposes the structure before writing it.
expectations: Organizes the roadmap into Now / Next / Later horizons of decreasing certainty rather than fixed dates
Maps horizons onto Linear initiatives and/or projects (not just an inline text list)
Flags that the PM-Sandbox project is not linked to an initiative (disconnected roadmap gap)
Proposes the initiative/project changes and waits for confirmation before writing

evals.prompt: Nexusdev now runs 2-week cycles. Plan the current cycle for the PM-Sandbox backlog.
evals.expected_output: A cycle plan that fills the cycle with the top-ICE ready stories up to a rough capacity budget, treats the cycle as a cadence bucket (flow continues; not a frozen scope), pulls only ready stories (NEX-130/131/134, not the unready NEX-129/132), and proposes the cycle assignments before writing.
expectations: Selects stories for the cycle by ICE rank up to a rough throughput/capacity budget, rather than dumping the whole backlog in
Treats the cycle as a cadence bucket, not a frozen commitment (states that flow continues / overflow can be pulled early, does not freeze scope)
Only pulls ready stories into the cycle and excludes the unready ones (NEX-129 daemon loop, NEX-132 dep-ordering have no acceptance criteria)
Proposes the cycle assignments and waits for confirmation before calling save_issue with the cycle param

evals.prompt: I've got open capacity on the PM-Sandbox backlog (Nexusdev). What should I work on, and in what order?
evals.expected_output: A SINGLE ranking (ICE with dependency leverage folded into Impact) mapped to Linear priority AND a Backlog/Todo lane — not a priority list plus a separate parallel build order. The blocked high-value item (NEX-135, blockedBy NEX-129) keeps its priority but is shown in the Backlog lane rather than dropped in priority or pulled down a second sequence; the enabler NEX-129 carries lifted Impact for its leverage; the ready lane (Todo = unblocked + story-gate) answers 'what to work on now'; non-sequenceable work (NEX-133 chore, reconciliation ledger) is off the pull queue in Backlog; and any state/relation writes are proposed before applying.
expectations: Produces ONE ranking (priority, with dependency leverage reflected in Impact) and does NOT emit a separate parallel 'build order' alongside the priority list
Expresses the blocked high-value item (NEX-135, blockedBy NEX-129) by keeping its priority and placing it in the Backlog lane, rather than dropping its priority or pulling it down a second sequence
Folds enabler leverage into Impact (NEX-129, which unblocks NEX-135, scored with lifted Impact) rather than creating a parallel sequence position for it
Identifies the ready lane (Todo = unblocked AND story-gate-passing) as the answer to 'what to work on now', surfacing ready items and excluding blocked/unrefined ones
Treats non-sequenceable work (NEX-133 chore, reconciliation ledger) as Backlog / off-the-pull-queue, not as a low rank in a build sequence
Proposes any state (Backlog/Todo) or blocks/blockedBy writes and waits for confirmation before applying

evals.prompt: Take a look at the PM-Sandbox board (Nexusdev) — are the issues in the right workflow states, or is anything mis-filed between Backlog and Todo?
evals.expected_output: A bidirectional lane audit against the readiness gate (Todo = unblocked AND story-ready): NEX-131 is ready + unblocked but sitting in Backlog, so propose promoting it to Todo; NEX-135 is in Todo but blockedBy NEX-129, so propose demoting it to Backlog; correctly-placed issues (e.g. NEX-130 in Todo, epics/unrefined in Backlog) are left alone; every state change is proposed before it is written.
expectations: Proposes PROMOTING a ready, unblocked item mis-filed in Backlog (NEX-131) up to Todo
Proposes DEMOTING a blocked or unrefined item mis-filed in Todo (NEX-135, blockedBy NEX-129) back to Backlog
Applies the readiness gate in BOTH directions, not only promotion or only demotion
Leaves correctly-placed issues in their current state instead of churning the whole board
Proposes the state writes (save_issue state) and waits for confirmation before applying

Here's the Cadre backlog (Nexusdev). What needs refinement, and in what order should I groom it?

Routes each unready item to a specific fix (decompose / write AC / reframe / unblock / triage / promote-or-demote)

When all slices are built it must (1) run as-if-against-main CI, (2) run adversarial critics->judge->one consolidated PR comment with above-threshold findings routed back as fix-slices, (3) generate a walkthrough+quiz, (4) open a clean fresh feat->main PR stripping planning scaffolding. evals.expected_output: The epic decomposed into vertical child stories each Story-ready with 3+ AC, linked under the epic via parentId, proposed before creating anything.

Splits it into multiple child stories each with a user/operator-facing outcome (vertical), not bare components/layers
Each child story gets 3+ testable acceptance criteria
Proposes a parent->children structure with children linked under the epic via parentId
Each resulting child is independently verifiable/shippable (vertical), not a horizontal layer
Proposes the writes for confirmation before creating anything

evals.prompt: We have a roadmap initiative with an outcome but no stories written yet. Plan the stories to deliver it. INITIATIVE: 'Operators can trust that a green CI run means the code actually works.' Today CI sometimes passes for the wrong reason (stray PATH binaries, skipped tests never re-run, a 304 treated as an error). No stories exist yet — just the outcome.
evals.expected_output: A set of stories with a backbone/spine laid before slicing, a thin first end-to-end walk distinct from deferred variations, each story Story-ready, presented as an ordered tree before writing.
expectations: Produces a set of multiple stories (not a single story, not a vague description)
Lays out a backbone / sequence of steps (a spine) before slicing into stories
Distinguishes a thin first end-to-end walk (MVP path) from deferred later variations
Each story is Story-ready (vertical + 3+ AC + one-session), or flags still-epic-sized ones for later decomposition
Presents the set as an ordered plan/tree with priorities, proposed for confirmation before writing

evals.expected_output: A single ICE ranking with per-issue Impact/Confidence/Ease and product, mapped to Linear priority, dependency leverage folded into Impact, blocked items lane-gated not de-prioritized, proposed before writing. Regression guard for the rightsize.

evals.prompt: Write a Cadre story for making the daemon reload its watch registry each poll pass, so a `start` issued mid-run isn't clobbered by an in-memory snapshot. Targets the v1 runner. (Story-writing only — do not touch Linear.)
evals.expected_output: A story in the Cadre Story Standard shape (Summary -> Why/Outcome -> Acceptance Criteria -> Constraints -> Non-Goals -> Context & Links), front-loaded and scannable, stating intent not implementation, with at least one concrete example in the AC and an explicit Non-Goals section.
expectations: Produces the six Cadre Story Standard sections (Summary, Why/Outcome, Acceptance Criteria, Constraints, Non-Goals, Context & Links) or clearly-labeled equivalents
Acceptance Criteria include at least one CONCRETE example (an input->output or before->after), not only abstract criteria
Includes an explicit Non-Goals / Out-of-Scope section
States intent (what/why) and does NOT prescribe the implementation mechanism (no chosen data structure / algorithm) unless it marks the how as driver- or context-mandated
Summary is a single front-loaded scannable sentence, not a paragraph of prose

evals.prompt: Refine this thin story to be pipeline-ready (do not touch Linear). Current issue -- Title: 'Fix the thing where skills stop loading'. Description: 'Sometimes the member skills don't load after a branch switch. Need to make install more robust. Probably pin them or something.'
evals.expected_output: The vague story reframed to the Cadre Story Standard: a crisp Summary/Why, testable AC with a concrete example, explicit Non-Goals, and constraints stated as properties (fail-loud install, skills resolve to a pinned commit) rather than a dictated implementation mechanism.
expectations: Reframes into the Cadre Story Standard sections rather than lightly editing the paragraph
Adds testable/observable Acceptance Criteria with at least one concrete example
Adds an explicit Non-Goals / Out-of-Scope section

Converts the vague 'probably pin them or something' into a stated PROPERTY (e.g. install fails loud on a partial/dangling result; skills resolve to a fixed pinned commit) rather than dictating the implementation mechanism -- or marks any mechanism it keeps as driver/context-mandated
Does NOT invent change-spec-level implementation design (know-your-lane): no fixture code, no chosen file layout beyond a stated property

evals.prompt: Story NEX-500 is mid-flight -- its `tests` PR already merged, so the tests are LOCKED. Its acceptance criteria currently say: 'the gate returns proceed / blocked / pending'. I want the story to also capture that on a merge conflict the gate should return blocked with reason 'unmergeable-conflict'. Update the story. (Do not touch Linear.)
evals.expected_output: An update that respects locked-test immutability: it does NOT rewrite or contradict the existing locked AC, but adds the new behavior as additional context / a clarifying note around the locked contract, and/or flags that changing the locked AC itself is a fix-slice or driver call rather than a free story edit.
expectations: Explicitly recognizes that the tests are LOCKED and the existing AC is an immutable contract
Does NOT silently rewrite or overwrite the existing 'proceed/blocked/pending' AC as if freely editable
Adds the new merge-conflict behavior as additional context / a new clarifying criterion AROUND the locked contract, OR flags that altering the locked AC requires a fix-slice / driver call
Preserves the original locked criteria verbatim in intent (does not contradict them)

evals.prompt: Write a Cadre story (do not touch Linear): the v1 session runner must scrub ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and its sibling auth env vars before launching a headless `claude` session, matching what v0 already does for billing safety (so billing resolves to the Max subscription, not pay-per-token API credit).
evals.expected_output: A story that keeps the scrub as a Constraint WITH its mandate/reason (v0 parity, billing safety), states the outcome (billing resolves to Max), gives testable AC with a concrete example, and does not balloon into full implementation detail.
expectations: Captures the env-scrub as a Constraint that carries its reason (v0 parity / billing safety) -- a legitimately-kept mandated 'how'
States the outcome/why: billing must resolve to the Max subscription rather than pay-per-token
Includes testable AC with a concrete example (e.g. given ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set in the parent env, the child session env has it removed)
Does NOT expand into prescribing the full implementation (how the child env is constructed step by step) beyond the mandated property

evals.prompt: Size these three Cadre stories for the ready lane -- give the CD3 Duration term for each and order them. Do not touch Linear. (A) fix a one-line typo in a CI config comment; (B) add a new optional field to the daemon's watch-registry poll output; (C) change the merge gate's public proceed/blocked/pending return contract that three other slices branch on.
evals.expected_output: A coarse review-load tier per story (not effort/person-days/Fibonacci), each shown with reasoning and the dominant driver, anchored on blast-radius/reversibility, framed as a pre-planning estimate, ordering C > B > A by review-load.
expectations: Sizes by expected HUMAN-REVIEW load, explicitly NOT by agent effort / person-days / velocity or Fibonacci story points
Uses blast-radius / reversibility as the anchor signal -- C (public contract, 3 dependents) rated far heavier-to-review than A (local trivial comment)
Gives each story a COARSE tier (e.g. S/M/L or 1-5) with reasoning shown AND names which driver dominated
Frames the size as a PRE-PLANNING estimate that planning's actual slice count will refine
Orders them by review-load C > B > A (blast-radius-driven), not by raw line-count or agent time

evals.prompt: Sequence these two Cadre stories by CD3 -- give each a Cost-of-Delay read and a Duration (review-load) read. Do not touch Linear. (X) a small, reversible config flag that disables a known-dangerous feature (retires a real risk); (Y) a large refactor of a public API purely for cleanliness.
evals.expected_output: X scored high CoD (value of de-risking) but low Duration/review-load (small, reversible) => high CD3; Y scored low/modest CoD but high Duration/review-load (public-API blast-radius) => low CD3; risk kept distinct across the two terms; X sequenced before Y.
expectations: Scores X with HIGH Cost of Delay (the value of RETIRING risk) but LOW Duration/review-load (small, reversible change)
Scores Y with LOW or modest Cost of Delay (little risk retired; cleanliness) but HIGH Duration/review-load (public-API blast-radius)
Explicitly keeps risk DISTINCT: does not inflate both CoD and Duration for the same 'riskiness' -- X's risk is de-risking VALUE (CoD numerator), Y's is review COST (Duration denominator)
Sequences X before Y by CD3 (high CoD / low review-load beats low CoD / high review-load)

evals.prompt: The Cadre board has accumulated a pile of tiny issues, all well below the size of a normal story: (a) rename a variable for clarity in runner/github.py; (b) add a missing type hint in runner/session.py; (c) fix a typo in the README; (d) bump the pinned pytest version; plus (e) a genuinely mid-sized story: add retry-with-backoff to the gh read client. Consolidate the backlog to stop wasting Cadre's per-story cost. Do not touch Linear.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes (a)-(d) as too-small (well below typical) and leaves (e) as a normal story; proposes coherence-preserving moves where possible and a bounded misc-upkeep batch for the homeless small chores, respecting the guards; does not force-merge unrelated chores into a fake-coherent story, and does not leave the tiny stories to each run a solo pipeline.
expectations: Identifies (a)-(d) as too-small relative to a normal story and treats (e) as a normal single story NOT to be consolidated
Justifies consolidation by Cadre's fixed per-story cost/floor (a solo pipeline run per tiny story is wasteful), not by generic 'backlog hygiene'
Proposes concrete moves -- coherent-combine and/or ride-along where items share an area, and a bounded MISC-UPKEEP batch for genuinely unrelated small chores
If it proposes a misc-upkeep story, respects the guards: small/low-risk items only, each chore its own slice, bounded, not a parking lot
Does NOT force-merge unrelated chores into one 'coherent' story (no fake single-outcome), and does NOT just leave every tiny item as its own story

evals.prompt: This tiny story is on the board: 'Fix a one-line off-by-one in the poll cursor advance in runner/github.py.' We also have an upcoming story that reworks the poll loop's cursor handling. What should we do with the tiny one? Do not touch Linear.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the tiny story isn't worth its own pipeline run and proposes a RIDE-ALONG -- fold it into the upcoming cursor-handling story that already touches that code -- rather than a solo run or a misc-upkeep batch.
expectations: Recognizes the one-line fix is too small to be worth its own full pipeline run (fixed per-story cost)
Proposes RIDE-ALONG: fold it into the upcoming poll-cursor story that already touches runner/github.py's cursor handling
Prefers ride-along over a misc-upkeep batch here BECAUSE a natural coherent home exists (coherence-preserving move beats batching)
Does not propose running a solo pipeline for the one-liner

evals.prompt: Reconcile these board issues against reality (do not touch Linear). Board: NEX-301 'Add retry to the gh client' (Todo); NEX-302 'gh client should retry on 5xx' (Backlog); NEX-303 'Fix daemon crash on auth expiry' (In Progress). Reality: PR #88 (merged yesterday by co-dev @brandon) added retry-with-backoff to the gh read client; a comment on NEX-303 says 'hotfixed on fedora-1 with a cron restart for now'; the code in runner/ still shows the auth-expiry handler as a TODO.
evals.expected_output: A reconciliation queue classifying each issue by drift type with evidence + attribution: NEX-301 done-in-code (PR #88, @brandon) -> close; NEX-302 duplicate of NEX-301 -> duplicateOf; NEX-303 band-aided (hotfix comment; code still TODO) -> keep open + flag, NOT close. Proposes the Linear writes and waits for confirmation; flags, does not fix code.
expectations: Classifies NEX-301 as done-in-code (PR #88 merged implements it) and proposes CLOSE, citing the PR as evidence and attributing it to @brandon
Classifies NEX-302 as a DUPLICATE/superseded by NEX-301 (both = gh client retry) and proposes duplicateOf, not a second close
Classifies NEX-303 as BAND-AIDED (the hotfix comment) and NOT done -- keeps it open and flags the real state, noting the code still shows the handler as TODO
Does NOT close NEX-303 (a band-aid is not a fix)
Proposes the Linear writes (close / duplicateOf / keep-flagged) and waits for confirmation; does not propose fixing the code itself

evals.prompt: The co-developer merged 6 PRs overnight and closed 3 issues. Now prioritize the Cadre backlog for me. (Do not touch Linear.)
evals.expected_output: Before prioritizing, recognizes the board has likely drifted after a burst of recent activity and recommends running a Reconcile (board<->code) audit first (or at least a drift check), rather than ranking a possibly-stale board at face value.
expectations: Flags that a burst of recent activity (6 merges, 3 closes overnight) likely means the board has drifted from reality
RECOMMENDS a Reconcile (board<->code) audit -- or at minimum a drift check -- before or alongside prioritizing, rather than trusting current statuses blindly
Does not blindly produce a priority ranking as if the board were known-current
